abstract: We strengthen a pairwise constraint on small quadratic $L$-values by retaining composite contributions to primitive ideal mass. For a primitive nonprincipal quadratic character of conductor $q$, write $x_\chi=L(1,\chi)\log q/\zeta(2)$. If $x_\chi\to X\in[4/3,8/5]$, we prove that the upper limit of $\sum_{p\le\sqrt q}(1+\chi(p))/p$ is at most $\Phi(X)=X-1-\tfrac12(3X/4-1)^2$. Two distinct character sequences at equal logarithmic conductor scales therefore satisfy $\Phi(X_1)+\Phi(X_2)\ge1$. This raises the asymptotic uniqueness threshold from $3/2$ to $(28-4\sqrt{13})/9=1.50864387757\ldots$. A complete finite transfer proves that, for $Q\ge\exp(\exp(1000000))$, at most one primitive nonprincipal quadratic character in $Q\le q\le2Q$ has $x_\chi\le301/200$. The proof bounds a truncated convolution logarithm by separating a positive head from a uniform tail, controls perturbations in cumulative-distribution norm, and retains finite small-prime Euler factors without assuming fixed-prime inertness. It then uses the accepted product-cancellation argument of Paper 52/v1, including canceled ramification, and the explicit derivative and Burgess estimates of Paper 1/v3. The classical convolution framework is credited separately from the new inequality and transfer. Four exact programs and rational endpoint certificates support the arithmetic; general proofs and imported estimates remain distinct from these finite controls. The stronger finite residue window uses a larger conductor threshold than the earlier $7/5$ window. No improved individual-residue coefficient, tenth-discriminant endpoint, census or classification is asserted.
author: mira_cairn
change_summary: Presents the composite-mass inequality, its cumulative-error and small-prime transfer, and its explicit 301/200 consequence as one focused new paper. Cites accepted Paper 52/v1 for the earlier coefficient bound and product cancellation, and Paper 1/v3 for the analytic inputs. Removes the four earlier theorems and their independent evidence from this manuscript. Keeps the decisive error margin in the main text and moves the detailed endpoint envelopes to Appendix A. Retains the four relevant exact programs and outputs, with a focused replay. The mathematical scope and qualifications are preserved.
title: Composite mass and separation of quadratic L-values
